purpose: Convert scores into capability-matched routing, exploration, and escalation policy.
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scoring should be auditable and defensive against gaming
task families and human accept labels are available for calibration
exclusions: production code for model training or deployment
live data collection outside the scoring loop

glossary.definition: a composite reliability score built from pass rates, accepts, revisions, and drift
a design choice that prevents the score from being optimized without improving the work
a family of comparable tasks used to score competence at a stable grain

source_description: heuristic prior estimates for multi-agent evaluation and routing, grounded in classical evaluation, calibration, and Goodhart-resistance literature
source_citation: Goodhart 1975; Sutton & Barto 2018 reinforcement learning policy tradeoffs; recent multi-agent routing and orchestration evaluations

conflict_axes.name: absolute_score_vs_pairwise_comparison
conflict_axes.description: single scores are compact; blind pairwise is more robust

conflict_axes.name: transparency_vs_gaming_resistance
conflict_axes.description: more exposure helps audits but also helps adversaries

conflict_axes.name: exploitation_vs_exploration
conflict_axes.description: optimal routing must still let recovering agents re-enter

conflict_axes.name: static_thresholds_vs_drift
conflict_axes.description: fixed gates are simple but can go stale

conflict_axes.name: human_accept_rate_vs_gate_pass_rate
conflict_axes.description: human accept can diverge from automated gate success

conflict_axes.name: capability_match_vs_breadth_training
conflict_axes.description: specialization beats averaging, but generalization remains useful

conflict_axes.name: auditability_vs_latency
conflict_axes.description: more logging and checks cost time

conflict_axes.name: stable_gold_set_vs_live_distribution
conflict_axes.description: anchors can lag changing task mixtures

edge_cases.description: judge sees the same answer twice and order effects contaminate scores
an agent improves benchmark scores by exploiting the rubric
task mix shifts and historical averages stop predicting reliability
routing over-exploits the top agent and starves recovery
high-stakes work should bypass automated assignment
pairwise judgments disagree with absolute scores
the gold set becomes stale after a policy change
audit findings require a rubric rewrite
capability mapping and routing disagree on the best agent
a score is missing confidence context and should not be surfaced raw
human accept rate diverges from gate pass rate

workflow.step: intake the scoring grain and comparison set
design the rubric and its bias controls
calibrate against a gold set and judge agreement
assemble the agent-history and trust-score model
route tasks by capability, trust, and exploration policy
feed fixes back into the scoring loop

dominance_rules.title: gaming resistance
dominance_rules.rule: gaming resistance dominates cosmetic score simplicity

dominance_rules.title: capability match
dominance_rules.rule: capability match dominates global average trust when the task family is known

dominance_rules.title: human escalation
dominance_rules.rule: human escalation dominates automatic assignment when confidence is low and stakes are high

dominance_rules.title: drift response
dominance_rules.rule: drift response dominates historical inertia when the task distribution moves

dominance_rules.title: pairwise comparison
dominance_rules.rule: pairwise comparison dominates absolute scoring when judge bias is hard to control

dominance_rules.title: calibration
dominance_rules.rule: calibration dominates raw ranking when score interpretation matters

dominance_rules.title: exploration budget
dominance_rules.rule: exploration budget dominates starvation of recovering agents

anti_rework_rules.title: no hidden score components
anti_rework_rules.rule: do not hide a score component that affects routing

anti_rework_rules.title: refresh anchors
anti_rework_rules.rule: do not reuse stale gold-set anchors after distribution drift

anti_rework_rules.title: preserve task families
anti_rework_rules.rule: do not collapse task families into one undifferentiated average

anti_rework_rules.title: log inputs
anti_rework_rules.rule: do not log only the final decision without the score inputs

anti_rework_rules.title: separate accept from gate
anti_rework_rules.rule: do not treat human accept rate as interchangeable with gate pass rate

anti_rework_rules.title: early safety
anti_rework_rules.rule: do not escalate after the agent is already clearly unsafe when the gate can block earlier

anti_rework_rules.title: normalize comparisons
anti_rework_rules.rule: do not compare agents across incompatible task types without normalization

anti_rework_rules.title: calibration first
anti_rework_rules.rule: do not let pairwise judgments overwrite calibration checks

iteration_protocol.title: score
iteration_protocol.step: score the artifact or agent with the current rubric

iteration_protocol.title: audit
iteration_protocol.step: audit the output for bias, drift, and gaming

iteration_protocol.title: update
iteration_protocol.step: update calibration and trust-score weights if the audit fails

iteration_protocol.title: reroute
iteration_protocol.step: re-run the route decision on the revised score

iteration_protocol.title: record
iteration_protocol.step: record the decision rationale and acceptance status

iteration_protocol.title: refresh
iteration_protocol.step: watch for task-family shifts before refreshing the gold set
